title: Prefill/Decode Conductor — adaptive kernel cascades and latency-contingent phase demotion
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: High-percentile latency spikes are occurring for mixed tenant workloads when the scheduler picks a single kernel variant early in the request lifecycle. Current prefill/decode policies favor static kernel assignment and coarse-grained phase splitting which leads to suboptimal tail behavior under bursty traffic.

Goal: Implement a Prefill/Decode Conductor that: 1) orchestrates an adaptive kernel cascade (multi-tier kernel candidates) across prefill and decode phases; 2) supports latency-contingent phase demotion where expensive decoding phases can be temporarily split or demoted based on latency headroom and tenant SLAs; 3) preserves tenant fairness and throughput by coupling cascade decisions with quota-aware soft limits.

Scope: design + prototype + limited rollout on dedicated staging pool. This ticket covers the scheduler and runtime hooks (kernel selection API, phase demotion signals, telemetry), not the user-facing console controls.

Non-goals: model re-compilation, quantization algorithm changes, or global routing/fallback policies outside the runtime node scope.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor accepts a ranked list of kernel candidates per model variant and dynamically promotes/demotes kernels at prefill/decode boundaries based on measured latency headroom.
Latency tail (p99) for mixed small/big context workloads decreases by >=12% on the staging pool compared to baseline when enabled with default policy.
Fairness metric (tenant-weighted slowdown) does not regress by more than 5% for high-priority tenants under the conductor policy.
End-to-end telemetry emitted: kernel_choice, phase_state (promoted/demoted), decision_reason, estimated_headroom_ms, and fallback_count; dashboards updated with these signals.
Prototype merged behind feature flag and smoke-tested on dedicated staging pool with canary rollout plan documented.
implementation_notes: Design a kernel candidate descriptor: (kernel_id, estimated_cost_tokens_per_ms, memory_profile, compatible_sequence_ranges).
Introduce Conductor decision loop executed at prefill completion and every decode phase boundary with a 1ms budget for decision-making; fallback to last-known good kernel if timeout.
Latency headroom estimation: combine per-tenant SLA deadline, current queue wait estimates, and observed per-token throughput samples to compute estimated_headroom_ms.
Phase demotion mechanism: allow splitting long decode phases into micro-phases (N tokens) and optionally switch to lighter kernel for remainder; ensure KV cache compatibility when switching kernels.
Fairness safeguard: enforce soft budget tokens per-tenant and implement a token-bucket backoff that reduces promoted kernel allocations when budget exhausted.
Telemetry: add structured tags to tracing spans (conductor.decision, kernel.candidate.rank, phase.action) and expose in Grafana.
comments: 2026-02-20 Priya Singh: Created ticket after incident investigation on 2026-02-18 (see incident postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident-2026-02-18-kernel-tail-spikes). Summary: prefill-decoder coupling caused cascade of expensive kernels under bursty prefill loads.

2026-02-25 Rafael Duarte: Ran initial microbenchmarks on model-llama-70b-qat; baseline p99 = 312ms, conductor prototype (static heuristic) p99 = 270ms. Saved ~13.5% tail latency. Benchmark details: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/sandbox/kernel-cascades?panelId=3

2026-03-01 Emily Chen (Senior SRE): Reviewed safety of dynamic kernel switching. Concern: KV cache layout differences may cause correctness regressions. ACTION: add compatibility matrix and fallback verification (unit test harness) — blocked until kernel metadata endpoint available (ENG-14207).

2026-03-03 Design review notes (Lina Park): UX for exposing 'latency headroom' knobs should default to conservative values. Recommend not exposing micro-phase length to customers initially; keep as runtime automatic policy. Link to design pad: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/UX/Conductor-UX

2026-03-07 Rafael Duarte: Implemented decision loop and added synthetic tests for kernel swap correctness. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345 — includes unit tests for KV cache version check and end-to-end smoke harness.

2026-03-09 Bench results on staging pool: mixed tenant run (50% small, 50% long): baseline p99=410ms, conductor adaptive cascade p99=356ms (-13.2%); throughput stable within 1.8% (measured tokens/s). Saved cost by demoting heavy kernel in 18% of long requests. Added raw csv artifacts to drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1fAj...
